vm_tools: concierge: do not keep xattrs/fflags in VM exports When exporting VMs, do not attempt to store extended attributes or "fflags" (chattr-style attributes). The files that are being archived should be normal files, aside from having the "encrypted" chattr flag set, which can't be preserved in an archive anyway. When libarchive adds files with these flags to a PAX-style tar file, it creates extra sections that GNU tar doesn't understand, which results in confusing error messages when extracting the tarball. Disable them to avoid adding the extra sections when using libarchive's "restricted pax" format so that the resulting tar file is cleanly extract-able with GNU tar and other tar implementations. cr50: use dedicated region for info1 accesses The INFO1 flash space is used for various purposes (endorsement key seed, Board ID and flags, serial number, etc.). Accessing these spaces in INFO1 is accompanied by managing the flash region registers, each time opening a window of the appropriate size, with appropriate permissions, etc, In fact none of these spaces contain a secret, to simplify things and preventing situations when concurrent accesses change the flash range window settings lets dedicate previously unused Region 7 register file to providing always open read access to INFO1. Write access will be enabled/disabled as required. In prod images write accesses will always happen from the vendor command context. In DBG images CLI commands will also have write access to INFO1. INFO1 window is accessed by other H1 based devices as well, this is why it is necessary to enable the window in the common chip code. crash-reporter: c++iza anomaly detector and have it use the journal Have anomaly_detector use the systemd journal as its log source instead of reading from /var/log/messages. Audit messages have been moved to /var/log/audit/audit.log, and attempts to make anomaly_detector read two files proved complicated: https://crrev.com/c/1630336 It was cleaner to completely rewrite anomaly detector by migrating it to C++ than to try to fit the current unit tests with the journal implementation. This has the added advantage of reducing the dependencies of the unit test and making it much faster since we no longer need to repeatedly call sleep. It's also now understood by the unit test framework as a group of multiple tests instead of one big test. Reading from journal has several advantages, most of which we aren't taking advantage of in this change, but can done in the future. Possible future improvements: * Use sd_journal_add_match and friends to make following the journal more efficient. * Save the journal cursor between boots to avoid missing certain early-boot and shutdown crashes: https://crbug.com/343954#c8 * Leverage structured audit data. Journald actually has all the audit fields we parse from the audit line as structured data. Use these instead of parsing the audit line. cryptohome: Add new commandline features for cryptohome commandline tool. To add new data restore key, simply type: cryptohome --action=add_data_restore_key --user=your_user_name Then type in your password, wait for a few second, then the hex string of data restore key will be displayed if authenticated. To build authentication, testers can use switch "--restore_key_in_hex" to provide data restore key in HexString, for instance if testers type: cryptohome --action=check_key_ex --user=your_user_name --restore_key_in_hex=0123456789ABCDEF Cryptohome will use restore key in AuthorizationRequest and check if it can be authenticated. To mass remove keys, users need to provide exempt key labels. Every other keyset whose label is not in exempt_key_labels will be removed. For instance, if users have four keysets which are labeled as "l1", "l2", "l3" and "l4", say if they want to delete l1 and l2 and keep l3 and l4, they should type: cryptohome --action=mass_remove_keys --user=your_user_name --exempt_key_labels=l3,l4 After authenticated, l1 and l2 will be removed. It will also allow us to probably extend that workaround for other platforms. net-print/ippusbxd: Adding exponential backoff for print read requests Initiating read requests uses an asynchronous callback system where requests are sent to the printer and then a callback will fire with the printer's response. If the printer currently has no data to service the read request then it responds with a 0-byte message. This system lead to ippusbxd spamming the printer continuously with read requests that came back with empty responses. shill: connection: Add oif rules for all interfaces Previously, a pair of iif rules were added for all physical interfaces. However, this still left an edge case in which a socket has SO_BINDTODEVICE but does not have bind() explicitly called. In this case, at connect() time, the socket is still implicitly bound to INADDR_ANY (for AF_INET sockets), and source address selection must occur. However, lacking any oif rules, our set of policy rules has nothing to distinguish this source address selection case from regular source address selection. Therefore when the socket is bound to a device that is not the primary interface on the system, the bound device and the outcome of source address selection are in disagreement. This change adds a pair of oif rules for all interfaces so that source address selection takes any potential bound device into account. Adding this functionality required providing support for FRA_OIFNAME in shill. Note that all of our kernel trees define this routing policy type.
